Solution B is correct. The count is 26 × 25 × 10 × 9. Since 26 × 25 = 650 and 10 × 9 = 90, the product is 650 × 90 = 58,500.

Solution A sets up the same product but makes an arithmetic error. It cancels one factor of 5 from 25 and one from 10, which is valid as far as it goes: 25 × 10 becomes 5 × 2 × 5 × ... but the cancellation was applied incorrectly. The step "26 times 5 times 2 times 9" equals 2340, which is 58,500 ÷ 25. The factor of 5 was dropped entirely instead of being kept in the product, so the result is too small by a factor of 25.

WINNER: B
